purpose: Define an optional, durable release-plan contract that lets a reviewed versioning decision be handed from planning to execution without treating a CI cache or an untracked workspace file as authoritative state.
scope: A versioned JSON VersionPlan and PublishPlan envelope, their CLI serialization and validation boundaries, and a deliberate plan-job to execute-job handoff. The core model is forge-neutral; the GitHub workflow is one adapter. This is an architecture change: the current single composite-action shell flow is not assumed to provide this boundary.
non_goals: Implementing a distributed transaction across registries, Git, and a forge.
Committing transient plan files, CI outputs, or caches to the repository.
Using a GitHub Actions cache as a correctness or recovery mechanism.
Replacing committed manifests, changelogs, release tags, or registry state as the durable records of a completed release.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The serialized envelope has explicit schema_version, source_commit, configuration_digest, input_digest, generation timestamp, and a payload containing planned package versions and ordered operations. For schema_version 1, both digests are lowercase SHA-256 hex of RFC 8785/JCS canonical JSON produced from named projection structs with every field present (including null); no digest is computed from a serde form with skip_serializing_if. ConfigurationDigestV1 contains the fully resolved release policy/configuration, with workspace-relative paths slash-normalized and unordered sets sorted by canonical key. InputDigestV1 contains source_commit, configuration_digest, accepted changeset identities plus content digests, and discovered package identities plus manifest content digests; ordered operations retain planner order. Unknown future schema versions and malformed/non-canonical digest fields are rejected before execution with an actionable diagnostic.

Execution accepts an explicit plan path or stdin and validates the envelope before any mutation. It fails before mutation when the checked-out source commit, configuration digest, input digest, or requested operation set differs from the plan; the diagnostic identifies every mismatching field.

Plans are emitted only on an explicit request. Local default commands leave no plan file behind. The GitHub adapter has an unprivileged plan job and a distinct protected execute job. The plan job uploads the explicit envelope with bounded retention and exposes its immutable artifact identifier and envelope digest as job outputs; the execute job downloads only that identifier from the same workflow run, verifies the digest, then validates the envelope before credentials are obtained. Other adapters provide an equivalent immutable run-scoped handoff. Caches may accelerate dependencies but are never a source of release intent.

A plan is safe to inspect, diff, archive, and regenerate: its domain types expose no credential, authorization-header, private-key, or arbitrary environment-value field, and plan generation neither reads nor serializes process environment. A serialization/schema test proves those structural constraints; a separate integration test injects secret-like environment values and proves the artifact contains none. Heuristic secret scanning may be defense in depth, but is not the correctness mechanism.

The plan/report distinguishes planned, attempted, completed, skipped, and failed operations. After an interrupted execution, a new invocation can produce a reconciliation report from repository, tag, and registry observations without assuming the old artifact is still available or correct.
